What it does is it protects persons with disabilities by supporting them in the exercise of their rights. And this is also true with respect of the right to equal recognition before the law. I see it in my own country, I see it in many civil law countries, and being a lawyer myself, I realize where it's coming from. It is a fundamental misunderstanding of the Convention to think that that substitute decision making is a means under the Convention to protect persons with disabilities. We need States parties need to change the system to a supported decision making system and provide the support necessary for persons with disabilities to take their decisions. And if they cannot express their will and preference, The support system needs to decide not in the best interest of the person, but based on the best available interpretation of that person's will and preference.
